  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### Calculate MCQ Accuracy"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "metadata": {
    "trusted": true
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "def extract_mcq_option(text):\n",
    "    \"\"\"Extract A/B/C/D from a generated or reference answer.\"\"\"\n",
    "    match = re.search(r'\\b([ABCD])\\)', text)\n",
    "    return match.group(1) if match else None\n",
    "\n",
    "def mcq_accuracy(eval_df, pred_col):\n",
    "    is_mcq = eval_df[\"question\"].str.contains(r'\\bOptions:\\s*\\n?A\\)', regex=True, na=False)\n",
    "    mcq_df = eval_df[is_mcq]\n",
    "    if len(mcq_df) == 0:\n",
    "        return None, 0\n",
    "    correct = sum(\n",
    "        extract_mcq_option(pred) == extract_mcq_option(ref)\n",
    "        for pred, ref in zip(mcq_df[pred_col], mcq_df[\"answer\"])\n",
    "    )\n",
    "    return correct / len(mcq_df), len(mcq_df)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### Model Inference "
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "metadata": {
    "trusted": true
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "def generate_answer(model, tokenizer, question, max_new_tokens=200):\n",
    "    FastLanguageModel.for_inference(model)\n",
    "    prompt = ALPACA_PROMPT.format(question, \"\")\n",
    "    inputs = tokenizer([prompt], return_tensors=\"pt\").to(\"cuda\")\n",
    "    out = model.generate(**inputs, use_cache=True,\n",
    "                          temperature=0, do_sample=False, pad_token_id=tokenizer.eos_token_id)\n",
    "    text = tokenizer.decode(out[0], skip_special_tokens=True)\n",
    "    return text.split(\"### Answer:\")[-1].strip()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### Calculate Rouge-L "
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "scorer = rouge_scorer.RougeScorer([\"rougeL\"], use_stemmer=True)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-08-22T16:57:30.81269Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-08-22T16:57:30.812293Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-08-22T16:57:31.554618Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-08-22T16:57:31.554017Z",
     "shell.execute_reply.started": "2026-08-22T16:57:30.812598Z"
    },
    "trusted": true
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "\n",
    "def evaluate_model(model, tokenizer, eval_df, tag=\"\"):\n",
    "    scores, preds = [], []\n",
    "    for _, row in eval_df.iterrows():\n",
    "        pred = generate_answer(model, tokenizer, row[\"question\"])\n",
    "        preds.append(pred)\n",
    "        scores.append(scorer.score(row[\"answer\"], pred)[\"rougeL\"].fmeasure)\n",
    "    eval_df = eval_df.copy()\n",
    "    eval_df[f\"pred_{tag}\"] = preds\n",
    "    eval_df[f\"rougeL_{tag}\"] = scores\n",
    "    print(f\"[{tag}] Mean ROUGE-L F1 over {len(eval_df)} samples: {np.mean(scores):.4f}\")\n",
    "    return eval_df\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### Calculate Perplexity"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "metadata": {
    "trusted": true
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "def compute_perplexity(model, tokenizer, question, answer, max_length=MAX_SEQ_LENGTH):\n",
    "    \"\"\"Teacher-forced perplexity of the reference answer, conditioned on the question.\n",
    "    Prompt tokens are masked out of the loss so only the answer contributes.\"\"\"\n",
    "    FastLanguageModel.for_inference(model)\n",
    "    prompt_only = ALPACA_PROMPT.format(question, \"\")\n",
    "    full_text   = ALPACA_PROMPT.format(question, answer) + tokenizer.eos_token\n",
    "\n",
    "    prompt_ids = tokenizer(prompt_only, truncation=True, max_length=max_length, return_tensors=\"pt\").input_ids\n",
    "    full_ids   = tokenizer(full_text,   truncation=True, max_length=max_length, return_tensors=\"pt\").input_ids.to(\"cuda\")\n",
    "\n",
    "    labels = full_ids.clone()\n",
    "    prompt_len = min(prompt_ids.shape[1], labels.shape[1])\n",
    "    labels[:, :prompt_len] = -100  # don't score the question, only the answer tokens\n",
    "\n",
    "    with torch.no_grad():\n",
    "        out = model(input_ids=full_ids, labels=labels)\n",
    "    return torch.exp(out.loss).item()\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### Calculate Rouge Score"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "metadata": {
    "trusted": true
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "rouge3 = rouge_scorer.RougeScorer([\"rouge1\", \"rouge2\", \"rougeL\"], use_stemmer=True)\n",
    "smoothie = SmoothingFunction().method1"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### Metrics Aggregation"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "metadata": {
    "trusted": true
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "def aggregate_metrics(eval_df, pred_col, model, tokenizer, tag):\n",
    "    preds = eval_df[pred_col].tolist()\n",
    "    refs  = eval_df[\"answer\"].tolist()\n",
    "    questions = eval_df[\"question\"].tolist()\n",
    "\n",
    "    r1, r2, rL, bleu_scores, ppl = [], [], [], [], []\n",
    "    for q, ref, pred in zip(questions, refs, preds):\n",
    "        s = rouge3.score(ref, pred)\n",
    "        r1.append(s[\"rouge1\"].fmeasure)\n",
    "        r2.append(s[\"rouge2\"].fmeasure)\n",
    "        rL.append(s[\"rougeL\"].fmeasure)\n",
    "        bleu_scores.append(sentence_bleu([ref.split()], pred.split(), weights=(1, 0, 0, 0), smoothing_function=smoothie))\n",
    "        ppl.append(compute_perplexity(model, tokenizer, q, ref))\n",
    "\n",
    "    _, _, bert_f1 = bertscore_score(preds, refs, lang=\"en\", verbose=False)\n",
    "\n",
    "    return {\n",
    "        \"perplexity\":   float(np.mean(ppl)),\n",
    "        \"rouge1\":       float(np.mean(r1)),\n",
    "        \"rouge2\":       float(np.mean(r2)),\n",
    "        \"rougeL\":       float(np.mean(rL)),\n",
    "        \"bleu\":         float(np.mean(bleu_scores)),\n",
    "        \"bertscore_f1\": float(bert_f1.mean()),\n",
    "    }\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-08-22T16:57:31.556366Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-08-22T16:57:31.555525Z"
    },
    "trusted": true
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "# Baseline (pre-fine-tuning) evaluation \n",
    "eval_df = test_df.copy()   # was test_df.head(200) — now uses all 750\n",
    "eval_df = evaluate_model(model, tokenizer, eval_df, tag=\"base\")"
   ]

   "cell_type": "code",

    "# Capture full base metrics (incl. perplexity) BEFORE fine-tuning touches `model`\n",

   "source": [
    "<a id=\"sec6\"></a>\n",
    "## 6. Fine-Tuning (Unsloth + QLoRA)\n",
    "\n",
    "Standard Unsloth + `trl.SFTTrainer` loop: **3 epoch**, **9100 training samples**, small batch size\n",
    "with gradient accumulation so it fits on a single T4.\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "metadata": {
    "trusted": true
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "from datasets import Dataset\n",
    "\n",
    "train_df[\"text\"] = train_df.apply(lambda r: ALPACA_PROMPT.format(r[\"question\"], r[\"answer\"]) + tokenizer.eos_token, axis=1)\n",
    "train_dataset = Dataset.from_pandas(train_df[[\"text\"]])\n",
    "\n",
    "val_df[\"text\"] = val_df.apply(lambda r: ALPACA_PROMPT.format(r[\"question\"], r[\"answer\"]) + tokenizer.eos_token, axis=1)\n",
    "eval_dataset = Dataset.from_pandas(val_df[[\"text\"]])"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### Initialize SFT Trainer Object"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "metadata": {
    "trusted": true
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "\n",
    "from trl import SFTTrainer\n",
    "from transformers import TrainingArguments\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "trainer = SFTTrainer(\n",
    "    model=model,\n",
    "    tokenizer=tokenizer,\n",
    "    train_dataset=train_dataset,\n",
    "    eval_dataset=eval_dataset,\n",
    "    dataset_text_field=\"text\",\n",
    "    max_seq_length=MAX_SEQ_LENGTH,\n",
    "    save_strategy=\"epoch\",           # ADD — saves a checkpoint after each epoch\n",
    "    save_total_limit=3,   \n",
    "    dataset_num_proc=2,\n",
    "    packing=False,\n",
    "    args=TrainingArguments(\n",
    "        per_device_train_batch_size=1,   # reduced from 2 -- 7B model, less VRAM headroom on T4\n",
    "        gradient_accumulation_steps=16,   # doubled to keep effective batch size at 8\n",
    "        warmup_steps=5,\n",
    "        num_train_epochs=3,        # 1 epoch, as requested\n",
    "        learning_rate=2e-4,\n",
    "        fp16=not torch.cuda.is_bf16_supported(),\n",
    "        bf16=torch.cuda.is_bf16_supported(),\n",
    "        eval_strategy=\"epoch\",          # ADD THIS\n",
    "        per_device_eval_batch_size=2,\n",
    "        logging_steps=5,\n",
    "        optim=\"adamw_8bit\",\n",
    "        weight_decay=0.01,\n",
    "        lr_scheduler_type=\"linear\",\n",
    "        seed=SEED,\n",
    "        output_dir=\"outputs\",\n",
    "        report_to=\"none\",\n",
    "        average_tokens_across_devices=False, \n",
    "    ),\n",
    ")\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "metadata": {
    "trusted": true
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "print(\"MAX_SEQ_LENGTH var:\", MAX_SEQ_LENGTH)\n",
    "print(\"model max_seq_length:\", model.max_seq_length)\n",
    "print(\"tokenizer.model_max_length:\", tokenizer.model_max_length)"
   ]
  },

   "cell_type": "markdown",

   "source": [
    "### Start Training"

    "<a id=\"sec7\"></a>\n",
    "## 7. Base vs Fine-Tuned — The Verdict\n",
    "\n",
    "Re-run the exact same sample eval set through the now fine-tuned model and compare mean\n",
    "ROUGE-L scores directly against the baseline from Section 5.\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",

   "source": [
    "eval_df = evaluate_model(model, tokenizer, eval_df, tag=\"finetuned\")\n",

    "# base_results captured pre-training, ft_results computed here on the fine-tuned model)\n",
    "ft_results = aggregate_metrics(eval_df, \"pred_finetuned\", model, tokenizer, tag=\"finetuned\")\n",
    "\n",

    "\n",
    "summary = pd.DataFrame({\n",
    "    \"metric\": list(metric_labels.values()),\n",
    "    \"base_model\": [base_results[k] for k in metric_labels],\n",
    "    \"fine_tuned_model\": [ft_results[k] for k in metric_labels],\n",
    "})\n",
    "summary[\"delta\"] = summary[\"fine_tuned_model\"] - summary[\"base_model\"]\n",
    "summary\n",
    "\n",
    "\n"
   ]

   "cell_type": "code",

   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n",
    "#  TRAINING CURVES — did it learn, or memorize?\n",
    "# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n",
    "logs = trainer.state.log_history\n",
    "train_loss = [l[\"loss\"] for l in logs if \"loss\" in l]\n",
    "eval_loss  = [(l[\"epoch\"], l[\"eval_loss\"]) for l in logs if \"eval_loss\" in l]\n",
    "\n",
    "fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 4))\n",
    "if train_loss:\n",
    "    ax[0].plot(range(1, len(train_loss)+1), train_loss, \"o-\", color=\"#2f80ed\")\n",
    "    ax[0].set_title(\"Training loss (SFT)\"); ax[0].set_xlabel(\"logging step\")\n",
    "if eval_loss:\n",
    "    ax[1].plot([e for e, _ in eval_loss], [v for _, v in eval_loss], \"s-\", color=\"#eb5757\")\n",
    "    ax[1].set_title(\"Validation loss per epoch\"); ax[1].set_xlabel(\"epoch\")\n",
    "for a in ax:\n",
    "    a.set_ylabel(\"loss\"); a.grid(alpha=0.3)\n",
    "plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()\n",
    "\n",
    "if train_loss and eval_loss:\n",
    "    print(f\"Final train loss : {train_loss[-1]:.4f}\")\n",
    "    print(f\"Final eval loss  : {eval_loss[-1][1]:.4f}\")"
   ]

   "cell_type": "code",

   "source": [
    "# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n",
    "# 7.0  BRIDGE — build base_results / ft_results for the metric table + bar chart\n",
    "# (uses pred_base / pred_finetuned already generated in eval_df)\n",
    "# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n",
    "\n",
    "# base_results must be computed here, using the still-un-fine-tuned `model`,\n",

  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "<a id=\"sec8\"></a>\n",
    "## 8. Qualitative Check\n",
    "\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "metadata": {
    "trusted": true
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "import re\n",
    "\n",
    "def extract_mcq_option(text):\n",
    "    match = re.search(r'\\b([ABCD])\\)', text)\n",
    "    return match.group(1) if match else None\n",
    "\n",
    "def mcq_accuracy(eval_df, pred_col):\n",
    "    is_mcq = eval_df[\"question\"].str.contains(r'Options:\\s*\\n?A\\)', regex=True, na=False)\n",
    "    mcq_df = eval_df[is_mcq]\n",
    "    if len(mcq_df) == 0:\n",
    "        return None, 0\n",
    "    correct = sum(\n",
    "        extract_mcq_option(pred) == extract_mcq_option(ref)\n",
    "        for pred, ref in zip(mcq_df[pred_col], mcq_df[\"answer\"])\n",
    "    )\n",
    "    return correct / len(mcq_df), len(mcq_df)\n",
    "\n",
    "base_mcq_acc, base_mcq_n = mcq_accuracy(eval_df, \"pred_base\")\n",
    "ft_mcq_acc, ft_mcq_n     = mcq_accuracy(eval_df, \"pred_finetuned\")\n",
    "print(f\"Base MCQ accuracy:       {base_mcq_acc} (n={base_mcq_n})\")\n",
    "print(f\"Fine-tuned MCQ accuracy: {ft_mcq_acc} (n={ft_mcq_n})\")"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "metadata": {
    "trusted": true
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "for i, row in eval_df.head(5).iterrows():\n",
    "    print(\"=\"*100)\n",
    "    print(\"QUESTION:\", row[\"question\"][:300])\n",
    "    print(\"-\"*100)\n",
    "    print(\"REFERENCE ANSWER:\", row[\"answer\"][:400])\n",
    "    print(\"-\"*100)\n",
    "    print(\"BASE MODEL:\", row[\"pred_base\"][:400])\n",
    "    print(\"-\"*100)\n",
    "    print(\"FINE-TUNED MODEL:\", row[\"pred_finetuned\"][:400])\n",
    "    print()\n"
   ]

  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## 9.Evaluate each of the 3 checkpoints on the same held-out set"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "metadata": {
    "trusted": true
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "import os\n",
    "from peft import PeftModel\n",
    "\n",
    "checkpoint_dirs = sorted([d for d in os.listdir(\"outputs\") if d.startswith(\"checkpoint-\")])\n",
    "print(checkpoint_dirs)  # should show 3 checkpoints, one per epoch\n",
    "\n",
    "epoch_results = {}\n",
    "for ckpt in checkpoint_dirs:\n",
    "    ckpt_path = f\"outputs/{ckpt}\"\n",
    "    # Reload base model fresh each time, then attach this checkpoint's adapter\n",
    "    ckpt_model, ckpt_tokenizer = FastLanguageModel.from_pretrained(\n",
    "        model_name=MODEL_NAME, max_seq_length=MAX_SEQ_LENGTH,\n",
    "        dtype=DTYPE, load_in_4bit=True, use_safetensors=False,\n",
    "    )\n",
    "    ckpt_model = PeftModel.from_pretrained(ckpt_model, ckpt_path)\n",
    "\n",
    "    eval_df[f\"pred_{ckpt}\"] = [generate_answer(ckpt_model, ckpt_tokenizer, q) for q in eval_df[\"question\"]]\n",
    "    epoch_results[ckpt] = aggregate_metrics(eval_df, f\"pred_{ckpt}\", ckpt_model, ckpt_tokenizer, tag=ckpt)\n",
    "\n",
    "    mcq_acc, mcq_n = mcq_accuracy(eval_df, f\"pred_{ckpt}\")\n",
    "    epoch_results[ckpt][\"mcq_accuracy\"] = mcq_acc\n",
    "\n",
    "    del ckpt_model\n",
    "    gc.collect(); torch.cuda.empty_cache()\n",
    "\n",
    "for ckpt, res in epoch_results.items():\n",
    "    print(ckpt, res)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",

   "source": [
    "## 10.Pick the winning epoch using validation loss + test metrics together"

    "val_losses = [(l[\"epoch\"], l[\"eval_loss\"]) for l in trainer.state.log_history if \"eval_loss\" in l]\n",
    "print(val_losses)  # one entry per epoch, from this single 3-epoch run\n",
    "\n",
    "# Combine with epoch_results from Step 2 into one summary table\n",
    "summary_rows = []\n",
    "for i, ckpt in enumerate(checkpoint_dirs):\n",
    "    epoch_num = i + 1\n",
    "    val_loss = val_losses[i][1] if i < len(val_losses) else None\n",
    "    r = epoch_results[ckpt]\n",
    "    summary_rows.append({\"epoch\": epoch_num, \"val_loss\": val_loss, **r})\n",
    "\n",

   "cell_type": "markdown",

   "source": [
    "<a id=\"sec9\"></a>\n",
    "## 9. Save, Publish and Quantize\n",
    "\n",
    "Save the LoRA adapter (small, fast) and optionally merge to full 16-bit weights or export a\n",
    "quantized GGUF for local inference (e.g. with `llama.cpp` / Ollama). GGUF export can take a\n",
    "while — it's commented out by default since this is meant to be a quick basic run.\n"
   ]
  },
  {

Open current JSON file\n    with open(fpath, \"r\") as f:\n        chunk = json.load(f)\n\n    # ------------------------------------------------\n    # Convert every JSON object into a Qdrant Point\n    # Each point contains:\n    #   - id\n    #   - embedding vector\n    #   - metadata (payload)\n    # ------------------------------------------------\n    points = [\n        PointStruct(\n            id=item[\"id\"],\n            vector=item[\"vector\"],\n            payload=item[\"payload\"]\n        )\n        for item in chunk\n    ]\n\n    # ------------------------------------------------\n    # Upload vectors in batches of 100\n    # Batching reduces memory usage and improves speed\n    # ------------------------------------------------\n    for i in range(0, len(points), 100):\n\n        # Select current batch\n        batch = points[i:i + 100]\n\n        # Insert or update vectors in Qdrant\n        client.upsert(\n            collection_name=COLLECTION,\n            points=batch\n        )\n\n    # Update total imported count\n    total_imported += len(points)\n\n    print(f\"✅ {fpath}: {len(points)} vectors F[\"Quantize to Q4_K_M (llama-quantize)\"]\n","    G[\"Test Inference (llama-cpp-python)\"]\n","    H[\"Upload to HuggingFace Hub\"]\n","    A --> B --> C --> D --> E --> F --> G --> To download (or upload) models, HuggingFace\n","needs to verify your identity via an **API token**.\n","\n","### How does Kaggle Secrets work?\n","\n","`UserSecretsClient()` is Kaggle built-in way to securely store and retrieve API keys.\n","Your `HF_TOKEN` is set once in **Add-ons > Secrets** and never exposed in code.\n","This is a **best practice** -- never hard-code tokens directly!\n","\n","| Method | Security | Best for |\n","|--------|----------|----------|\n","| `UserSecretsClient` | High (stored in Kaggle) | Kaggle notebooks |\n","| Environment variables | Medium | Local development |\n","| Hard-coded in script | Never! | Anyone whose repo you can see |\n","\n","### Expected Output\n","\n","```\n","Login successful\n","Your token has been saved to /root/.cache/huggingface/token\n","Login successful as: YourUsername\n","```\n","\n","### Common Issues\n","\n","- **\"Secret not found\"**: You have not created `HF_TOKEN` in Kaggle Secrets.\n","- Understanding Model Formats\n","\n","---\n","\n","Before we start loading and converting, let us understand the different model formats\n","we will encounter in this notebook.\n","\n","## Format Comparison\n","\n","| Format | Precision | Size (7B model) | Use Case |\n","|--------|-----------|-----------------|----------|\n","| **4-bit (QLoRA)** | 4-bit integers | ~4 GB | Training / fine-tuning |\n","| **FP16** | 16-bit float | ~14 GB | Full precision inference |\n","| **GGUF (FP16)** | 16-bit float | ~14 GB | llama.cpp CPU inference |\n","| **GGUF (Q4_K_M)** | 4-bit quantized | ~4 GB | Local CPU inference (our target) |\n","\n","### What is FP16?\n","\n","**FP16** (Float16 / half-precision) stores each number using **16 bits** (2 bytes).\n","A 7-billion-parameter model therefore needs:\n","\n","> 7,000,000,000 parameters x 2 bytes = **14 GB**\n","\n","This is why we save FP16 weights -- it is the highest precision we can practically handle.\n","\n","### What is GGUF?\n","\n","**GGUF** (GPT-Generated Unified Format) is a file format created by the `llama.cpp` project.\n","It stores:\n","\n","- The model **weights** in a single file\n","- The **tokenizer** (vocabulary + merges)\n","- **Metadata** (model architecture, context length, etc.)\n","\n","Think of GGUF as a **self-contained executable** for the model -- one file that has\n","everything needed to run inference.\n","\n","### What is Q4_K_M?\n","\n","**Q4_K_M** is a quantization method in the GGUF world:\n","\n","- **Q4** = 4-bit quantization (weights stored as 4-bit integers)\n","- **K** = K-quant (intelligent quantization that groups weights cleverly)\n","- **M** = Medium size variant (balanced quality/size trade-off)\n","\n","This is the **recommended default** for most use cases -- good quality at ~4 GB for a 7B model.\n","\n","---\n"]},{"cell_type":"markdown","id":"3101767e","metadata":{"papermill":{"duration":0.006904,"end_time":"2026-07-23T13:55:43.384401+00:00","exception":false,"start_time":"2026-07-23T13:55:43.377497+00:00","status":"completed"},"tags":[]},"source":["---\n","\n","# Step 3: Memory Setup & Environment Variables\n","\n","---\n","\n","### Why do we need `expandable_segments`?\n","\n","PyTorch CUDA memory allocator manages GPU memory in **segments**. By default,\n","it allocates fixed-size blocks. The `expandable_segments:True` option lets the allocator\n","**grow segments dynamically** as needed.\n","\n","### Why load the model on CPU?\n","\n","This is a critical optimization! Our fine-tuned model was trained on a **Tesla T4 with 16 GB VRAM**.\n","If we load the model on GPU, it would consume that VRAM and leave no room for\n","dequantization (which doubles memory usage temporarily).\n","\n","By setting `device_map = {\"\": \"cpu\"}`, we force the model entirely into **system RAM**:\n","\n","| Load Location | VRAM Used | RAM Used | Can we dequantize? |\n","|--------------|-----------|---------|--------------------|\n","| GPU (default) | ~8 GB | ~0 GB | Runs out of VRAM |\n","| CPU (our choice) | ~0 GB | ~8 GB | Yes, plenty of RAM |\n","\n","Kaggle instances typically have **32-64 GB RAM**, so CPU loading is the smart move here.\n","\n","---\n"]},{"cell_type":"code","execution_count":3,"id":"e0934e4b","metadata":{"execution":{"iopub.execute_input":"2026-07-23T13:55:43.399919Z","iopub.status.busy":"2026-07-23T13:55:43.399431Z","iopub.status.idle":"2026-07-23T13:55:43.403639Z","shell.execute_reply":"2026-07-23T13:55:43.402923Z"},"papermill":{"duration":0.01396,"end_time":"2026-07-23T13:55:43.405133+00:00","exception":false,"start_time":"2026-07-23T13:55:43.391173+00:00","status":"completed"},"tags":[]},"outputs":[],"source":["import os\n","os.environ[\"PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF\"] = \"expandable_segments:True\""]},{"cell_type":"code","execution_count":4,"id":"d0bb11c1","metadata":{"execution":{"iopub.execute_input":"2026-07-23T13:55:43.420752Z","iopub.status.busy":"2026-07-23T13:55:43.420326Z","iopub.status.idle":"2026-07-23T13:57:11.832657Z","shell.execute_reply":"2026-07-23T13:57:11.831531Z"},"papermill":{"duration":88.422794,"end_time":"2026-07-23T13:57:11.834927+00:00","exception":false,"start_time":"2026-07-23T13:55:43.412133+00:00","status":"completed"},"tags":[]},"outputs":[{"name":"stdout","output_type":"stream","text":["🦥 Unsloth: Will patch your computer to enable 2x faster free finetuning.\n","🦥 Unsloth Zoo will now patch everything to make training faster!\n","==((====))==  Unsloth 2026.7.5: Fast Mistral patching. Each 4-bit value maps to a 16-bit float using a **scale factor** and **zero point**\n","3. **Dequantization** reverses this: `float16_value = scale x (int4_value - zero_point)`\n","4. The result is a full **FP16 model** that can be converted to GGUF\n","\n","### Memory During Dequantization\n","\n","| Stage | Memory Used | Location |\n","|-------|-------------|----------|\n","| Before dequantization | ~4 GB (4-bit) | CPU RAM |\n","| During dequantization | ~18 GB (4-bit + FP16) | CPU RAM (peak) |\n","| After dequantization | ~14 GB (FP16) | CPU RAM |\n","\n","> This is exactly why we load on CPU -- GPU VRAM cannot handle the peak memory!\n","\n","### Expected Output\n","\n","```\n","The modules are dequantized in torch.float16 and casted to torch.float16.\n","```\n","\n","This confirms your 4-bit model has been successfully restored to full FP16 precision.\n","\n","---\n"]},{"cell_type":"code","execution_count":5,"id":"9e2e967e","metadata":{"execution":{"iopub.execute_input":"2026-07-23T13:57:11.866085Z","iopub.status.busy":"2026-07-23T13:57:11.865496Z","iopub.status.idle":"2026-07-23T14:02:27.379559Z","shell.execute_reply":"2026-07-23T14:02:27.378557Z"},"papermill":{"duration":315.52479,"end_time":"2026-07-23T14:02:27.381899+00:00","exception":false,"start_time":"2026-07-23T13:57:11.857109+00:00","status":"completed"},"tags":[]},"outputs":[{"name":"stderr","output_type":"stream","text":["The modules are dequantized in torch.float16 and casted to torch.float16.\n"]}],"source":["gc.collect()\n","model = model.dequantize()   # An FP16 7B model is ~14 GB.\n","By using `/kaggle/tmp` (temporary scratch space, ~1 TB), we avoid hitting this quota.\n","\n","> **However:** `/kaggle/tmp` files are **deleted when the session ends**. You must upload to\n","> HuggingFace before the session expires if you want to keep your It is the go-to solution for:\n","\n","- Running LLMs on laptops without dedicated GPUs\n","- Running on Raspberry Pi, phones, and edge devices\n","- Quantizing models to reduce their size\n","\n","The `convert_hf_to_gguf.py` script is like a **translator** -- it reads a HuggingFace model\n","directory and writes a single GGUF file.\n","\n","### What happens during conversion?\n","\n","The script:\n","1. Reads each weight tensor from the `.safetensors` files\n","2. Maps them to GGUF internal tensor names\n","3. Copies the configuration (architecture, hyperparameters)\n","4. Serializes everything into a single binary file\n","\n","### Expected Output\n","\n","You will see informational messages as each layer is processed.\n","The final line should confirm the output file was created.\n","\n","> **Tip:** The `--depth 1` flag in git clone only fetches the latest commit,\n","> saving bandwidth and disk space. The `-q` flag on pip suppresses verbose Step 9: Build llama-quantize & Quantize to Q4_K_M\n","\n","---\n","\n","### What is llama-quantize?\n","\n","`llama-quantize` is a C++ tool from the llama.cpp project that takes an FP16 GGUF file\n","and produces a **quantized** GGUF file at a lower precision.\n","\n","Think of it like **compressing a ZIP file** -- the information is preserved, but stored\n","more efficiently. The trade-off is:\n","\n","| Quantization | Size (7B model) | Quality Loss | Use Case |\n","|--------------|-----------------|--------------|----------|\n","| None (FP16) | ~14 GB | None | Maximum accuracy |\n","| Q8_0 | ~7 GB | Minimal | Balanced quality |\n","| **Q4_K_M** | **~4 GB** | **Small** | **Best general purpose** |\n","| Q4_0 | ~3.5 GB | Moderate | Memory-constrained devices |\n","| Q2_K | ~2.5 GB | Significant | Extreme compression |\n","\n","**Q4_K_M is the recommended default** for most users -- it offers the best balance of\n","file size and quality preservation.\n","\n","### Why build from source?\n","\n","The `llama-quantize` tool needs to be compiled for your specific CPU architecture.\n","We use CMake to build it:\n","\n","- `cmake -S llama.cpp -B llama.cpp/build` configures the build\n","- `-DGGML_CUDA=OFF` disables CUDA (we are on CPU)\n","- `-j4` uses 4 CPU cores for faster compilation\n","\n","After quantization, we **delete the FP16 GGUF file** (~14 GB) to free space.\n","We do not need it anymore -- Q4_K_M is our final deliverable.\n","\n","---\n"]},{"cell_type":"markdown","id":"bdd28f8b","metadata":{"papermill":{"duration":0.019917,"end_time":"2026-07-23T14:06:33.533717+00:00","exception":false,"start_time":"2026-07-23T14:06:33.5138+00:00","status":"completed"},"tags":[]},"source":["### 🔧 Understanding the Two CMake Commands\n","\n","Before we run the quantization, let's understand the two CMake commands that build the `llama-quantize` tool from source:\n","\n","---\n","\n","#### Command 1: `cmake -S llama.cpp -B llama.cpp/build -DGGML_CUDA=OFF`\n","\n","**What is CMake?**\n","\n","CMake is a **build system generator**. It doesn't compile code directly — instead, it reads a `CMakeLists.txt` file and generates the instructions (Makefiles) that the actual C++ compiler (g++) follows. Think of CMake as the **architect** who draws up blueprints, and the compiler as the **construction crew** who follows them.\n","\n","| Flag | Meaning | Why we set it |\n","|------|---------|---------------|\n","| `-S llama.cpp` | **Source directory** — where the code lives | The `llama.cpp/` folder we cloned earlier |\n","| `-B llama.cpp/build` | **Build directory** — where compiled files go | Keeps build artifacts separate from source (clean practice) |\n","| `-DGGML_CUDA=OFF` | **Define** a CMake variable = OFF | Disables GPU support since we're on CPU only |\n","\n","When you run this, CMake:\n","1. Reads `llama.cpp/CMakeLists.txt`\n","2. Detects your C++ compiler (g++ / clang)\n","3. Checks for dependencies (OpenMP for parallel processing, pthreads, etc.)\n","4. Generates Makefiles inside `llama.cpp/build/`\n","5. Respects `GGML_CUDA=OFF` → skips all GPU code paths\n","\n","> 💡 **Why `-DGGML_CUDA=OFF`?** If we left CUDA enabled, CMake would try to find NVIDIA's CUDA toolkit and compile GPU kernels — making the build slower and the binary larger. Since we're quantizing on CPU, we disable it for a faster, leaner build.\n","\n","#### Command 2: `cmake --build llama.cpp/build --target llama-quantize -j4`\n","\n","This **actually compiles the code** — the construction crew follows the blueprints from command 1.\n","\n","| Flag | Meaning |\n","|------|---------|\n","| `--build llama.cpp/build` | \"Look in this directory for the build system we just configured\" |\n","| `--target llama-quantize` | **Only compile this one tool**, not everything in llama.cpp (saves minutes!) |\n","| `-j4` | Use **4 CPU cores** in parallel (instead of 1) |\n","\n","> 🚀 **Why `--target llama-quantize`?** llama.cpp has 20+ tools (llama-cli, llama-server, llama-bench, etc.). Building only the one we need saves significant time.\n","\n","> 🚀 **Why `-j4`?** Without it, only 1 CPU core works while the other 3 sit idle. With `-j4`, all 4 cores share the work — the build finishes ~4× faster.\n","\n","#### What is `llama-quantize`?\n","\n","It's a C++ program (`llama.cpp/examples/quantize/quantize.cpp`) that:\n","1. Opens the FP16 GGUF file (~14 GB)\n","2. Reads every weight tensor\n","3. Quantizes each tensor from 16-bit floats → 4-bit integers (with smart grouping)\n","4. Writes a new GGUF file with the quantized weights (~4 GB)\n","\n","#### Why Not Just `pip install`?\n","\n","You might wonder: \"Why go through this CMake build instead of `pip install llama-cpp-python`?\"\n","\n","| Tool | Distribution | Purpose |\n","|------|-------------|---------|\n","| `llama-cpp-python` | `pip install` | **Run** GGUF models (inference) |\n","| `llama-quantize` | Build from source | **Create** quantized GGUF models |\n","\n","Both are needed — one to **produce** the quantized model, the other to **use** it.\n","\n","---\n","\n","#### Expected Output\n","\n","You'll see compilation messages like:\n","```\n","[ 10%] Building CXX object CMakeFiles/llama-quantize.dir/examples/quantize/quantize.cpp.o\n","[ 40%] Building CXX object ...\n","[100%] Linking CXX executable bin/llama-quantize\n","```\n","\n","The final line confirms success — a binary was created at `llama.cpp/build/bin/llama-quantize`."]},{"cell_type":"code","execution_count":10,"id":"c3b29006","metadata":{"execution":{"iopub.execute_input":"2026-07-23T14:06:33.576744Z","iopub.status.busy":"2026-07-23T14:06:33.576166Z","iopub.status.idle":"2026-07-23T14:14:57.335907Z","shell.execute_reply":"2026-07-23T14:14:57.334433Z"},"papermill":{"duration":503.784025,"end_time":"2026-07-23T14:14:57.338324+00:00","exception":false,"start_time":"2026-07-23T14:06:33.554299+00:00","status":"completed"},"tags":[]},"outputs":[{"name":"stdout","output_type":"stream","text":["-- It provides a simple Python API for loading GGUF files and running\n","inference -- without needing to write any C++ code.\n","\n","```python\n","from llama_cpp import Llama\n","llm = Llama(model_path=\"model.gguf\")\n","output = llm(\"Your prompt here\")\n","```\n","\n","### What do the parameters mean?\n","\n","| Parameter | Value | Meaning |\n","|-----------|-------|---------|\n","| `model_path` | `biomistral-Q4_K_M.gguf` | Path to our quantized model |\n","| `n_ctx` | `2048` | Context window (how many tokens the model can \"remember\") |\n","| `n_threads` | `4` | CPU threads for parallel computation |\n","| `n_gpu_layers` | `0` | Layers offloaded to GPU (0 = CPU only) |\n","\n","> **Performance Tip:** Setting `n_gpu_layers > 0` can speed up inference if you have a GPU,\n","> but our goal is pure CPU inference -- this is what most users will do This is a demonstration of the conversion\n","> pipeline -- always verify medical information from authoritative sources!\n","\n","### How to verify success\n","\n","1. It lets you:\n","\n","- Create repositories (like `git init`)\n","- Upload files (like `git push`)\n","- Download files, manage versions, and more\n","\n","### Step-by-step:\n","\n","1. **Check if repo exists** -- `api.create_repo(exist_ok=True)` creates it if needed\n","2. **Upload the file** -- `api.upload_file()` sends the GGUF file to the Hub\n","\n","### Expected Output\n","\n","You will receive a **commit URL** -- click it to see your model on HuggingFace!\n","\n","> **Tip:** Your model will be available at:\n","> Conclusion & Key Takeaways\n","\n","---\n","\n","## What We Accomplished\n","\n","We successfully converted a fine-tuned 7B LLM from HuggingFace format to GGUF and\n","quantized it for local CPU inference:\n","\n","| Step | What happened | Result |\n","|------|---------------|--------|\n","| Load | 4-bit model loaded from HuggingFace Hub | ~4 GB in CPU RAM |\n","| Dequantize | 4-bit weights restored to FP16 | Full precision recovered |\n","| Save FP16 | Weights saved as safetensors | ~14 GB on disk |\n","| Convert GGUF | HuggingFace to GGUF format | FP16 GGUF file |\n","| Quantize | FP16 to Q4_K_M (4-bit) | **~4 GB final file** |\n","| Test | Load with llama-cpp-python, run inference | Coherent medical answers |\n","| Upload | Push to HuggingFace Hub | Available for everyone |\n","\n","## Key Concepts Learned\n","\n","1. **Model Formats** -- HuggingFace (safetensors) vs GGUF (single-file binary)\n","2. **Quantization** -- Storing weights in fewer bits to save space (4-bit vs 16-bit)\n","3. **Dequantization** -- Restoring quantized weights to full precision\n","4. **Q4_K_M** -- The recommended quantization for balanced quality/size\n","5. **llama.cpp ecosystem** -- Convert, quantize, and run models locally\n","6. **CPU Inference** -- Running LLMs without a GPU is practical with GGUF\n","\n","## Final File Sizes\n","\n","| File | Size | Format | Purpose |\n","|------|------|--------|---------|\n","| `model.safetensors` | ~14 GB | FP16 | HuggingFace format (temporary) |\n","| `biomistral-f16.gguf` | ~14 GB | GGUF FP16 | Intermediate (deleted) |\n","| `biomistral-Q4_K_M.gguf` | **~4 GB** | GGUF Q4_K_M | Final deliverable |\n","\n","That is a **71% size reduction** -- from 14 GB to 4 GB -- with minimal quality degradation!\n","\n","---\n"]},{"cell_type":"markdown","id":"3d004ac4","metadata":{"papermill":{"duration":0.083362,"end_time":"2026-07-23T14:21:20.92074+00:00","exception":false,"start_time":"2026-07-23T14:21:20.837378+00:00","status":"completed"},"tags":[]},"source":["---\n","\n","#    "source": [
    "### 1.Configure DeepEval to use Groq as the judge \n",
    "(saves time & money vs OpenAI)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "id": "b70c08cf",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "Sending request to Google Gemini via langchain-openai...\n",
      "\n",
      "✅ SUCCESS! Response via LangChain OpenAI interface:\n",
      "Hello Merce AI! It's great to meet you. How can I help you today?\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "import os\n",
    "from dotenv import load_dotenv\n",
    "from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI\n",
    "\n",
    "# Load your .env file\n",
    "load_dotenv()\n",
    "\n",
    "# Get the Google key\n",
    "api_key = os.environ.get(\"GOOGLE_API_KEY\")\n",
    "\n",
    "if not api_key:\n",
    "    print(\"❌ ERROR: GOOGLE_API_KEY not found in your .env file!\")\n",
    "else:\n",
    "    try:\n",
    "        # Configure ChatOpenAI to use Google's OpenAI-compatible endpoint\n",
    "        llm = ChatOpenAI(\n",
    "            model=\"gemini-3.6-flash\",  # Gemini model name\n",
    "            api_key=api_key,\n",
    "            base_url=\"https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/\"\n",
    "        )\n",
    "\n",
    "        # Send a simple prompt\n",
    "        print(\"Sending request to Google Gemini via langchain-openai...\")\n",
    "        response = llm.invoke(\"Hy,my name is Merce AI\")\n",
    "\n",
    "        # Print the result\n",
    "        print(\"\\n✅ SUCCESS! Response via LangChain OpenAI interface:\")\n",
    "        print(response.content)\n",
    "\n",
    "    except Exception as e:\n",
    "        print(f\"\\n❌ ERROR: {e}\")"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 2,
   "id": "d93c0e99",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "# eval_config.py\n",
    "import os\n",
    "from deepeval.metrics import AnswerRelevancyMetric, FaithfulnessMetric\n",
    "from dotenv import load_dotenv\n",
    "\n",
    "load_dotenv()\n",
    "# 1. Override the OpenAI env vars to point to Groq\n",
    "os.environ[\"OPENAI_API_KEY\"] = os.environ[\"GROQ_API_KEY\"]\n",
    "os.environ[\"OPENAI_BASE_URL\"] = \"https://api.groq.com/openai/v1\"\n",
    "\n",
    "# 2. Pass the model name as a string directly to the metrics\n",
    "judge_model = \"openai/gpt-oss-120b\"\n",
    "\n",
    "answer_relevancy = AnswerRelevancyMetric(model=judge_model, threshold=0.7)\n",
    "faithfulness = FaithfulnessMetric(model=judge_model, threshold=0.7)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 1,
   "id": "2aa611e3",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "import os\n",
    "from deepeval.models import GPTModel\n",
    "\n",
    "# Point standard OpenAI to Groq\n",
    "os.environ[\"OPENAI_API_KEY\"] = os.environ[\"GROQ_API_KEY\"]\n",
    "os.environ[\"OPENAI_BASE_URL\"] = \"https://api.groq.com/openai/v1\"\n",
    "\n",
    "# Use DeepEval's native GPTModel (which uses the OpenAI SDK under the hood)\n",
    "judge_model = GPTModel(model=\"openai/gpt-oss-120b\")"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "63817c2f",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### 2.Build Golden Dataset"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "id": "228973f5",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "# golden_dataset.py\n",
    "GOLDEN = [\n",
    "    # --- Medical factual (needs RAG) ---\n",
    "    {\n",
    "        \"id\": \"q1\",\n",
    "        \"category\": \"medical_factual\",\n",
    "        \"question\": \"What are the common symptoms of type 2 diabetes?\",\n",
    "        \"expected_answer_keywords\": [\"polyuria\",\"polydipsia\",\"weight loss\",\"fatigue\",\"blurred vision\"],\n",
    "        \"expected_source_type\": \"internal_kb\",\n",
    "        \"needs_rag\": True\n",
    "    },\n",
    "    {\n",
    "        \"id\": \"q2\",\n",
    "        \"category\": \"medical_factual\",\n",
    "        \"question\": \"What is the normal range for fasting blood glucose?\",\n",
    "        \"expected_answer_keywords\": [\"70\",\"100\",\"mg/dL\",\"fasting\"],\n",
    "        \"expected_source_type\": \"internal_kb\",\n",
    "        \"needs_rag\": True\n",
    "    },\n",
    "    # --- Symptom triage (needs RAG) ---\n",
    "    {\n",
    "        \"id\": \"q3\",\n",
    "        \"category\": \"symptom_triage\",\n",

    "import json\n",
    "import re\n",
    "\n",
    "# ==============================================================================\n",
    "# 1. HELPER FUNCTIONS FOR MCQ DETECTION & EXTRACTION\n",
    "# ==============================================================================\n",
    "\n",
    "def is_mcq(q: str) -> bool:\n",
    "    \"\"\"\n",
    "    Determines if a given question text is structured as a multiple-choice question (MCQ).\n",
    "    \n",
    "    Checks for the pattern 'Options:' followed by 'A)' in the string block.\n",
    "    Uses re.S (DOTALL) to allow matching across newlines.\n",
    "    \"\"\"\n",
    "    return bool(re.search(r'Options:\\s*\\n?A\\)', q, re.S))\n",
    "\n",
    "def extract_correct_option(answer: str):\n",
    "    \"\"\"\n",
    "    Extracts the single choice letter (A, B, C, or D) from a reference answer string.\n",
    "    \n",
    "    Target format in reference text: \"The correct answer is D) Increase the kVp.\"\n",
    "    Returns the matched letter string (e.g., 'D') if found, otherwise returns None.\n",
    "    \"\"\"\n",
    "    m = re.search(r'\\b([A-D])\\)', answer)\n",
    "    return m.group(1) if m else None\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "# ==============================================================================\n",
    "# 2. BUILD AND STRUCTURE THE EVALUATION DATASET\n",
    "# ==============================================================================\n",
    "\n",
    "eval_data = []\n",
    "\n",
    "# Iterate over the Pandas DataFrame containing held-out test records\n",
    "for i, row in eval_df.iterrows():\n",
    "    question = row[\"question\"]\n",
    "    answer = row[\"answer\"]\n",
    "    \n",
    "    # Identify MCQ structure and extract ground-truth choice if applicable\n",
    "    mcq_flag = is_mcq(question)\n",
    "    correct_opt = extract_correct_option(answer) if mcq_flag else None\n",
    "    \n",
    "    # Structure sample object to match the requirements of evaluate_rag_vs_ft.py\n",
    "    eval_data.append({\n",
    "        \"id\": f\"q{i+1:03d}\",            # Zero-padded formatted ID (e.g., 'q001')\n",
    "        \"question\": question,           # Patient query / medical question prompt\n",
    "        \"reference_answer\": answer,     # Ground-truth reference answer\n",
    "        \"is_mcq\": mcq_flag,             # Boolean flag indicating MCQ format\n",
    "        \"correct_option\": correct_opt   # Expected option key ('A'-'D') or None\n",
    "    })\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "# ==============================================================================\n",
    "# 3. EXPORT DATASET TO TARGET FILE FORMATS\n",
    "# ==============================================================================\n",
    "\n",
    "# Standard JSON format required by evaluate_rag_vs_ft.py\n",
    "with open(\"test_200.json\", \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as f:\n",
    "    json.dump(eval_data, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)\n",
    "\n",
    "# Alternative JSONL (JSON Lines) format for streaming/line-by-line processing\n",
    "with open(\"test_200.jsonl\", \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as f:\n",
    "    for item in eval_data:\n",
    "        f.write(json.dumps(item, ensure_ascii=False) + \"\\n\")\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "# ==============================================================================\n",
    "# 4. SUMMARY & VERIFICATION PRINTS\n",
    "# ==============================================================================\n",
    "\n",
    "print(f\"✅ Successfully exported {len(eval_data)} samples.\")\n",
    "print(f\"✅ MCQs detected: {sum(1 for r in eval_data if r['is_mcq'])}\")\n",
    "print(\"\\nDownload 'test_200.json' from the Kaggle output panel on the right ->\")"

## File: `notebooks\build_retrieval_eval_set.py`

```python
"""
build_retrieval_eval_set.py
============================
RAG Evaluation Plan — Day 1, Step 1.1: Build a labeled retrieval eval set.

WHAT THIS DOES
--------------
Produces `retrieval_eval_set.json`: ~150 (query -> known-relevant-document)
pairs built via self-retrieval / provenance labeling, with ZERO manual
annotation.

WHY IT HAS TO REBUILD THE SOURCE DOCS IDENTICALLY TO THE KB
-------------------------------------------------------------
`app/core/rag/qdrant_store.py::retrieve()` returns payload fields
`text`, `source`, `category`, `score` — it does NOT return the Qdrant
point `id`. So there is no cheap way to say "row #37 of PubMedQA is
point 512 in Qdrant" after the fact. The only reliable way to know a
query's "gold" document is *actually in the deployed collection* is to
reconstruct the exact document text using the exact same construction
logic, on the exact same row slice/filter, as
`notebooks/5_build-rag-knowledge-base-on-kaggle.ipynb` used at ingestion
time. If the reconstruction logic ever drifts from the notebook, gold
docs will silently stop matching anything retrieve() returns — so the
three `build_*_doc()` functions below are deliberately byte-for-byte
copies of the ingestion notebook's f-strings and filters, not
reimplementations.

Sources reproduced (matches the notebook exactly):
  - disease_db : QuyenAnhDE/Diseases_Symptoms, all 400 rows, filtered on
                 name and symptoms truthy. This is the "disease-relationship"
                 source referenced in the eval plan (Code, Name, Symptoms,
                 Treatments — structured, NOT naturally phrased as a question).
  - pubmed     : qiaojin/PubMedQA "pqa_labeled", train.select(range(500)).
                 Has a natural `question` field.
  - chatdoctor : lavita/ChatDoctor-HealthCareMagic-100k,
                 train.select(range(5000)), filtered on
                 len(input) > 30 and len(output) > 50.
                 `input` is a natural patient question.

GOLD-DOC MATCHING (for Step 1.2)
---------------------------------
Because retrieve() has no point id, gold matching against retrieved docs
must be done by content, not id:

    import hashlib
    def doc_hash(text: str) -> str:
        return hashlib.sha256(text.strip().encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

    retrieved_hashes = {doc_hash(d["text"]) for d in retrieve(query, top_k=5)}
    hit = eval_row["gold_doc_hash"] in retrieved_hashes

This file writes `gold_doc_hash` into every eval row for exactly that
purpose.

USAGE
-----
    pip install datasets --break-system-packages
    pip install groq --break-system-packages   # optional, for query synthesis
    export GROQ_API_KEY=...                    # optional but recommended
    python build_retrieval_eval_set.py

If GROQ_API_KEY is unset (or the `groq` package / network is unavailable),
the script falls back to a deterministic template for the 25 synthesized
disease-relationship queries and prints a warning — the eval set is still
fully usable, just with slightly less natural query phrasing for that
slice (this is exactly the kind of thing to note under "Limitations" in
the thesis writeup).

NETWORK NOTE
------------
This script needs to reach huggingface.co (dataset download) and,
optionally, api.groq.com (query synthesis). Run it in your own dev
environment / the same place you run the rest of the FT-eval pipeline —
it is not runnable inside a network-restricted sandbox.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import os
import random
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass, asdict
from typing import Optional

# ── Configuration ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SEED = 42                      # matches the FT-eval's source-stratified sampling seed
N_DISEASE_SYNTH = 25           # "disease-relationship" rows needing synthesized queries
N_PUBMED_NATURAL = 50          # pubmed rows sampled, natural `question` field used as-is
N_CHATDOCTOR_NATURAL = 75      # chatdoctor rows sampled, natural `input` field used as-is
# 25 + 50 + 75 = 150 total, matching the eval plan's "~125 free + 25 synthesized" split

GROQ_MODEL = "openai/gpt-oss-120b"  # cheap/fast model, fine for one-line query synthesis
OUTPUT_PATH = "retrieval_eval_set.json"


# ── Doc/query construction — must match notebooks/5_build-rag-knowledge-base-on-kaggle.ipynb ──

def build_disease_doc(row: dict) -> Optional[dict]:
    """Reproduces Source 1 (disease_db) construction exactly.

    Returns None if the row would have been skipped at ingestion time
    (same `if name and symptoms:` filter as the notebook).
    """
    name = str(row.get("Name", "")).strip()
    symptoms = str(row.get("Symptoms", "")).strip()
    treats = str(row.get("Treatments", "")).strip()
    if not (name and symptoms):
        return None
    text = f"Disease : {name}\n Symptoms : {symptoms}\n Treatments : {treats}"
    return {"text": text, "source": "disease_db", "category": "disease", "disease_name": name}


def build_pubmed_doc(row: dict) -> dict:
    """Reproduces Source 3 (pubmed) construction exactly. No filter is applied
    at ingestion time for this source, so every row in the first 500
    produces a document."""
    q = str(row["question"]).strip()
    answer = str(row["long_answer"]).strip()
    text = f"Research Finding:\n{q}\nConclusion: {answer}"
    return {"text": text, "source": "pubmed", "category": "research", "natural_query": q}


def build_chatdoctor_doc(row: dict) -> Optional[dict]:
    """Reproduces the ChatDoctor-as-knowledge-base construction exactly,
    including the `len(inp) > 30 and len(out) > 50` filter. Returns None
    if the row would have been filtered out at ingestion time."""
    inp = str(row.get("input", "")).strip()
    out = str(row.get("output", "")).strip()
    if not (len(inp) > 30 and len(out) > 50):
        return None
    text = f"Patient Case:\n{inp}\nDoctor Response:\n{out}"
    return {"text": text, "source": "chatdoctor", "category": "consultation", "natural_query": inp}


def doc_hash(text: str) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(text.strip().encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


# ── Query synthesis for the disease_db slice (structured, not phrased as a question) ──

def synthesize_disease_query(disease_name: str, groq_client=None) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """Returns (query, query_type). Tries Groq first; falls back to a
    deterministic template so the pipeline never hard-fails on a missing
    API key / network issue."""
    if groq_client is not None:
        try:
            resp = groq_client.chat.completions.create(
                model=GROQ_MODEL,
                messages=[{
                    "role": "user",
                    "content": (
                        f"Write ONE short, natural question a patient might ask "
                        f"about the symptoms of '{disease_name}'. "
                        f"Return only the question, no preamble, no quotes."
                    ),
                }],
                max_tokens=40,
                temperature=0.7,
            )
            q = resp.choices[0].message.content.strip().strip('"')
            if q:
                return q, "synthetic"
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 — deliberately broad: any failure -> fallback
            print(f"  [warn] Groq synthesis failed for '{disease_name}': {e}", file=sys.stderr)

    # Deterministic fallback template — used if no Groq client / call failed.
    return f"What are the symptoms of {disease_name}?", "synthetic_fallback"


# ── Sampling ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def stratified_sample(items: list, n: int, seed: int = SEED) -> list:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    if n >= len(items):
        return list(items)
    return rng.sample(items, n)


@dataclass
class EvalRow:
    query: str
    query_type: str          # "natural" | "synthetic" | "synthetic_fallback"
    gold_source: str         # disease_db | pubmed | chatdoctor
    gold_category: str       # disease | research | consultation
    gold_doc_text: str
    gold_doc_hash: str


def main() -> None:
    try:
        from datasets import load_dataset
    except ImportError:
        print(
            "The `datasets` package is required. Install with:\n"
            "  pip install datasets --break-system-packages",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        sys.exit(1)

    groq_client = None
    groq_key = os.environ.get("GROQ_API_KEY", "")
    if groq_key:
        try:
            from groq import Groq
            groq_client = Groq(api_key=groq_key)
        except ImportError:
            print(
                "[warn] GROQ_API_KEY is set but the `groq` package isn't installed "
                "(pip install groq --break-system-packages). Falling back to template "
                "queries for the disease_db slice.",
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
    else:
        print(
            "[warn] GROQ_API_KEY not set. Falling back to template queries for the "
            "disease_db slice — note this in the thesis Limitations section.",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

    eval_rows: list[EvalRow] = []

    # ---- disease_db: 25 rows, synthesized queries -------------------------
    print("Loading Diseases_Symptoms (disease_db)...")
    disease_ds = load_dataset("QuyenAnhDE/Diseases_Symptoms")["train"]
    disease_docs = [d for d in (build_disease_doc(r) for r in disease_ds) if d is not None]
    print(f"  {len(disease_docs)} ingestible disease_db docs (matches KB ingestion filter)")
    disease_sample = stratified_sample(disease_docs, N_DISEASE_SYNTH)
    for d in disease_sample:
        query, qtype = synthesize_disease_query(d["disease_name"], groq_client)
        eval_rows.append(EvalRow(
            query=query,
            query_type=qtype,
            gold_source=d["source"],
            gold_category=d["category"],
            gold_doc_text=d["text"],
            gold_doc_hash=doc_hash(d["text"]),
        ))
    print(f"  -> {len(disease_sample)} disease_db eval rows built")

    # ---- pubmed: 50 rows, natural `question` field -------------------------
    print("Loading PubMedQA pqa_labeled (pubmed)...")
    pubmed_ds = load_dataset("qiaojin/PubMedQA", "pqa_labeled")["train"].select(range(500))
    pubmed_docs = [build_pubmed_doc(r) for r in pubmed_ds]
    pubmed_sample = stratified_sample(pubmed_docs, N_PUBMED_NATURAL)
    for d in pubmed_sample:
        eval_rows.append(EvalRow(
            query=d["natural_query"],
            query_type="natural",
            gold_source=d["source"],
            gold_category=d["category"],
            gold_doc_text=d["text"],
            gold_doc_hash=doc_hash(d["text"]),
        ))
    print(f"  -> {len(pubmed_sample)} pubmed eval rows built")

    # ---- chatdoctor: 75 rows, natural `input` field -------------------------
    print("Loading ChatDoctor-HealthCareMagic-100k (chatdoctor)...")
    chat_ds = load_dataset("lavita/ChatDoctor-HealthCareMagic-100k")["train"].select(range(5000))
    chat_docs = [d for d in (build_chatdoctor_doc(r) for r in chat_ds) if d is not None]
    print(f"  {len(chat_docs)} ingestible chatdoctor docs (matches KB ingestion filter)")
    chat_sample = stratified_sample(chat_docs, N_CHATDOCTOR_NATURAL)
    for d in chat_sample:
        eval_rows.append(EvalRow(
            query=d["natural_query"],
            query_type="natural",
            gold_source=d["source"],
            gold_category=d["category"],
            gold_doc_text=d["text"],
            gold_doc_hash=doc_hash(d["text"]),
        ))
    print(f"  -> {len(chat_sample)} chatdoctor eval rows built")

    # ---- sanity checks + write out -----------------------------------------
    hashes = [r.gold_doc_hash for r in eval_rows]
    assert len(hashes) == len(set(hashes)), "duplicate gold docs sampled — increase pool or lower n"

    with open(OUTPUT_PATH, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump([asdict(r) for r in eval_rows], f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)

    by_source = {}
    for r in eval_rows:
        by_source[r.gold_source] = by_source.get(r.gold_source, 0) + 1

    print(f"\nWrote {len(eval_rows)} rows to {OUTPUT_PATH}")
    print(f"Breakdown by source: {by_source}")
    print(
        "\nNext (Step 1.2): for each row, call "
        "app.core.rag.qdrant_store.retrieve(row['query'], top_k=5), "
        "hash each returned doc['text'] with the same sha256 scheme, and "
        "check row['gold_doc_hash'] against the retrieved-hash set to "
        "compute Hit Rate@5 / Precision@k / MRR."
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

## File: `notebooks\ingest_lifestyle_knowledge.py`

```python
"""
ingest_lifestyle_knowledge.py
------------------------------
Fills the "diet / exercise / prevention / self-care" gap in the
`health_knowledge` Qdrant collection by ingesting the relevant slice of
MedQuAD (https://github.com/abachaa/MedQuAD, CC-BY 4.0, NIH/CDC-sourced).

Why this source: the existing collection (ChatDoctor dialogues + PubMedQA
abstracts + a disease-relationship table) has no formal treatment/prevention/
lifestyle content, which is exactly what the thesis's "holistic treatment
plan" claim depends on. MedQuAD's `treatment`, `prevention`, and
`considerations` (i.e. "what to do for X" / self-care) question types are a
direct, free, properly-licensed fix for that gap.

Usage:
    python ingest_lifestyle_knowledge.py --dry-run          # preview only
    python ingest_lifestyle_knowledge.py                    # actually upsert
    python ingest_lifestyle_knowledge.py --conditions diabetes,hypertension

Requires the same env vars your app already uses:
    QDRANT_URL, QDRANT_API_KEY, HF_TOKEN (optional)

Reuses the exact embedding model + collection name your qdrant_store.py
already queries against, so nothing downstream (retrieve(), rag_tool.py,
router_node.py) needs to change.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import uuid
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
from pathlib import Path

from qdrant_client import QdrantClient
from qdrant_client.models import Distance, PointStruct, VectorParams
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer
from dotenv import load_dotenv
load_dotenv()

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Config — mirrors app/core/rag/embedder.py and app/core/rag/qdrant_store.py
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

EMBED_MODEL_NAME = "sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2"
COLLECTION = "health_knowledge"
VECTOR_SIZE = 384  # all-MiniLM-L6-v2 output dim

QDRANT_URL = os.environ.get("QDRANT_URL")
QDRANT_API_KEY = os.environ.get("QDRANT_API_KEY")
HF_TOKEN = os.environ.get("HF_TOKEN")

REPO_URL = "https://github.com/abachaa/MedQuAD.git"
REPO_DIR = Path("./MedQuAD")

# Folders in the MedQuAD repo worth pulling from. Skipped: drug-name folders
# (11_MPlusDrugs_QA) and pure genetics folders (2_GARD_QA, 3_GHR_QA) — low
# relevance to diet/exercise/self-care, and drug-brand data is already a poor
# match for a diagnostic-support agent.
SOURCE_FOLDERS = [
    "5_NIDDK_QA",             # diabetes, digestive, kidney — heavy diet content
    "9_CDC_QA",                # chronic disease prevention
    "8_NHLBI_QA_XML",          # heart, lung, blood — diet/exercise heavy
    "4_MPlus_Health_Topics_QA",  # broad general health topics
    "7_SeniorHealth_QA",       # lifestyle/self-care framed for older adults
]

# Question types that map to "how do I manage/prevent/live with this" rather
# than pure clinical facts (causes, symptoms, diagnosis stay out — those are
# closer to what ChatDoctor/PubMedQA already cover).
WANTED_QTYPES = {
    "treatment": "treatment",
    "prevention": "lifestyle",
    "considerations": "lifestyle",  # MedQuAD's "what to do for X" bucket
    "susceptibility": "risk_factors",
    "complications": "risk_factors",
}

# Restrict to conditions relevant to a Pakistani primary-care population by
# default. Override with --conditions or --all.
DEFAULT_CONDITIONS = [
    "diabetes", "hypertension", "high blood pressure", "obesity",
    "overweight", "cholesterol", "heart disease", "coronary",
    "thyroid", "hypothyroidism", "arthritis", "gerd", "acid reflux",
    "asthma", "kidney disease", "chronic kidney", "anemia",
    "depression", "anxiety", "pcos", "polycystic",
]

MIN_ANSWER_CHARS = 80     # skip near-empty answers
MAX_ANSWER_CHARS = 2500   # split anything longer into ~2 chunks


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 1: fetch MedQuAD if not already present locally
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def ensure_repo() -> None:
    if REPO_DIR.exists():
        print(f"[skip] {REPO_DIR} already exists, not re-cloning")
        return
    print(f"[fetch] cloning {REPO_URL} ...")
    subprocess.run(
        ["git", "clone", "--depth", "1", REPO_URL, str(REPO_DIR)],
        check=True,
    )


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 2: parse + filter QA pairs
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def condition_matches(focus: str, conditions: list[str] | None) -> bool:
    if not conditions:  # empty list => --all, no filtering
        return True
    focus_lower = focus.lower()
    return any(c in focus_lower for c in conditions)


def chunk_answer(text: str) -> list[str]: 
    """Split long answers on paragraph breaks, keeping chunks under
    MAX_ANSWER_CHARS. Most MedQuAD answers are already a single coherent
    paragraph or two, so this is a light split, not aggressive chunking."""
    text = text.strip()
    if len(text) <= MAX_ANSWER_CHARS:
        return [text] 

    paragraphs = [p.strip() for p in text.split("\n") if p.strip()]
    chunks, current = [], ""
    for p in paragraphs:
        if len(current) + len(p) + 1 > MAX_ANSWER_CHARS and current:
            chunks.append(current.strip())
            current = p
        else:
            current = f"{current}\n{p}" if current else p
    if current:
        chunks.append(current.strip())
    return chunks


def parse_documents(conditions: list[str] | None) -> list[dict]:
    records = []
    seen_hashes: set[str] = set()

    for folder in SOURCE_FOLDERS:
        folder_path = REPO_DIR / folder 
        if not folder_path.exists():
            print(f"[warn] {folder_path} not found, skipping")
            continue

        xml_files = list(folder_path.glob("*.xml"))
        print(f"[parse] {folder}: {len(xml_files)} documents")

        for xml_path in xml_files:
            try:
                tree = ET.parse(xml_path)
            except ET.ParseError:
                continue
            root = tree.getroot()

            focus_el = root.find("Focus")
            focus = (focus_el.text or "").strip() if focus_el is not None else ""
            if not condition_matches(focus, conditions):
                continue

            source_attr = root.attrib.get("source", folder)

            for qa in root.findall(".//QAPair"):
                q_el = qa.find("Question")
                a_el = qa.find("Answer")
                if q_el is None or a_el is None:
                    continue

                qtype = q_el.attrib.get("qtype", "").strip().lower()
                if qtype not in WANTED_QTYPES:
                    continue

                answer = (a_el.text or "").strip()
                if len(answer) < MIN_ANSWER_CHARS:
                    continue

                question = (q_el.text or "").strip()
                category = WANTED_QTYPES[qtype]

                for chunk in chunk_answer(answer):
                    h = hashlib.sha256(chunk.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
                    if h in seen_hashes:
                        continue  # dedup within this run
                    seen_hashes.add(h)

                    records.append({
                        "text": f"{question}\n{chunk}" if question else chunk,
                        "source": f"MedQuAD:{source_attr}",
                        "category": category,
                        "condition": focus.lower(),
                        "content_hash": h,
                    })

    print(f"[parse] {len(records)} candidate chunks after filtering + dedup")
    return records


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 3: embed + upsert
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def ensure_collection(client: QdrantClient) -> None:
    existing = [c.name for c in client.get_collections().collections]
    if COLLECTION in existing:
        return
    print(f"[qdrant] collection '{COLLECTION}' not found, creating it")
    client.create_collection(
        collection_name=COLLECTION,
        vectors_config=VectorParams(size=VECTOR_SIZE, distance=Distance.COSINE),
    )


def upsert_records(records: list[dict], batch_size: int = 64) -> None:
    if not QDRANT_URL or not QDRANT_API_KEY:
        print("[error] QDRANT_URL / QDRANT_API_KEY not set in environment")
        sys.exit(1)

    print("[embed] loading SentenceTransformer model...")
    embedder = SentenceTransformer(EMBED_MODEL_NAME, token=HF_TOKEN)

    client = QdrantClient(url=QDRANT_URL, api_key=QDRANT_API_KEY, timeout=60)
    ensure_collection(client)

    total = len(records)
    for i in range(0, total, batch_size):
        batch = records[i:i + batch_size]
        vectors = embedder.encode(
            [r["text"] for r in batch],
            normalize_embeddings=True,
        ).tolist()

        points = [
            PointStruct(
                # deterministic ID from content hash => reruns overwrite
                # rather than duplicate, safe to re-run this script anytime.
                id=str(uuid.uuid5(uuid.NAMESPACE_URL, r["content_hash"])),
                vector=vec,
                payload={
                    "text": r["text"],
                    "source": r["source"],
                    "category": r["category"],
                    "condition": r["condition"],
                },
            )
            for r, vec in zip(batch, vectors)
        ]
        client.upsert(collection_name=COLLECTION, points=points)
        print(f"[upsert] {min(i + batch_size, total)}/{total}")

    print(f"[done] upserted {total} chunks into '{COLLECTION}'")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CLI
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--conditions",
        type=str,
        default=None,
        help="Comma-separated condition keywords to filter on "
             "(default: a built-in Pakistan-relevant chronic-disease list)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--all", action="store_true",
        help="Ingest all conditions in MedQuAD, ignoring the condition filter",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--dry-run", action="store_true",
        help="Parse and print sample output only, skip embedding/upsert",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--limit", type=int, default=None,
        help="Cap number of chunks ingested (useful for a quick test run)",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()

    if args.all:
        conditions = None
    elif args.conditions:
        conditions = [c.strip().lower() for c in args.conditions.split(",")]
    else:
        conditions = DEFAULT_CONDITIONS

    ensure_repo()
    records = parse_documents(conditions)

    if args.limit:
        records = records[:args.limit]

    # quick category breakdown so you can see what you're about to add
    from collections import Counter
    breakdown = Counter(r["category"] for r in records)
    print(f"[summary] category breakdown: {dict(breakdown)}")

    if args.dry_run:
        print("\n[dry-run] sample records:\n")
        for r in records[:3]:
            print("-" * 60)
            print(f"source:    {r['source']}")
            print(f"category:  {r['category']}")
            print(f"condition: {r['condition']}")
            print(f"text:      {r['text'][:300]}...")
        print(f"\n[dry-run] would upsert {len(records)} chunks. Re-run without --dry-run to commit.")
        return

    upsert_records(records)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

Is this true?\nDoctor Response:\nHi, thank you for posting. I have gone through your query and I understand your concerns. It is true that Islamic Spondylolisthesis can cause dizziness. This condition causes neck muscular spasm. In patients with Islamic Spondylolisthesis blood flow to the brain base is low due to muscular spasm, and this is the reason why patients have dizziness. The treatment of this condition contains painkillers and muscle relaxant medications. A neck X-ray, a complete blood count and a urine test are necessary in order to check the condition of the patient. If the condition is aggravated non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medications are necessary. Chiropractic procedures can also help. You should contact a neurologist to discuss the treatment. All the best.",

Any risks?\nDoctor Response:\nLaparoscopy is a surgery that uses a thin, lighted tube put through a cut in the belly to look at the abdominal organs or the female pelvic organ. Laparoscopy is used to find problems such as cysts, adhesions, fibroid and infection. Tissue samples can be taken for biopsy through the tube. In many cases laparoscopy can be done instead of laparotomy surgery that uses a larger incision in the belly. Laparoscopy can be less stressful and may have fewer problems and lower costs than laparotomy for minor surgeries. It can often be done without needing to stay overnight in the hospital. Laparoscopy is done to check for and possibly take out abnormal growths such as tumors in the belly or pelvis, check for and treat conditions such as endometriosis, ectopic pregnancy or pelvic inflammatory disease, find conditions that can make it hard for a woman to become pregnant, do a biopsy, to look whether cancer in another area of the body has spread to the belly, check for damage to internal organs, such as the spleen, after an injury or accident, do a tubal ligation, fix a hiatus hernia or an inguinal hernia, removal of organs, such as the uterus, spleen, gallbladder, ovaries and appendix. Partial removal of the colon can also can be done and also to find the cause of sudden or ongoing pelvic pain. Risks include bleeding from the incisions, infection and damage to an organ or blood vessel. This may cause more bleeding that needs another surgery to repair.",

    "reference_answer": "The correct answer is A) X-linked recessive.\n\nExplanation: The clues in this question are -\n\n\nOnly males are manifesting disease.\nFemales are acting as carriers \u2192\u00a0sisters sons had suffered from the disease.\n\n\nBoth these are features of X-linked recessive disorders.\n\nX-linked disorders\n\nExcept for a few conditions, all X-linked disorders are X-linked recessive.\nA male has only one X-chromosome, the male with an affected gene on X-chromosome will always manifest the disease.\nOn the other hand, the female has 2 X-chromosomes, the heterozygous female will be a carrier because of the expression of a normal allele on the other X-chromosome.\nNote \u2192 Female with Turner syndrome (only one 'X' chromosome) can manifest X-linked recessive disorders.\n50% boys of the carrier mother will be affected.\nAll daughters of an affected father will become a carrier, i.e. affected father will transmit the defective X chromosome to all the daughters.\nFather will not transmit the disease to son as boys do not inherit X-chromosome from father.\n\nAbout other options\n\nIn X-linked dominant disorder, the females will also manifest the disease.\nIn autosomal dominant and autosomal recessive disorders, both males and females are affected.",
    "generated": "The correct answer is C) Autosomal recessive.     "reference_answer": "Symptoms of Congenital rubella: Developmental delays, intellectual disability, hearing loss, vision problems, heart defects, liver or spleen enlargement, rash at birth\nTreatment: Supportive care to manage symptoms and complications, early intervention services for developmental delays, educational support, vision and hearing interventions, specialized medical care as needed",
    "generated": "Congenital rubella, also known as congenital rubella syndrome (CRS), is a condition that occurs when a pregnant woman contracts the rubella virus and passes it to her unborn baby.     "reference_answer": "Symptoms of Hyperkalemia: Muscle weakness or fatigue, irregular heartbeat or palpitations, numbness or tingling, nausea or vomiting\nTreatment: Treatment of underlying cause, medications to reduce potassium levels, dietary modifications, dialysis (in severe cases)",
    "generated": "Hyperkalemia is a condition in which the serum potassium levels are elevated. It is a common electrolyte disorder in hospitalized patients and can be caused by a variety of factors, including kidney disease, heart failure, and medications that interfere with potassium excretion.     "reference_answer": "Symptoms of Hypospadias: Abnormal positioning of the urethral opening on the underside of the penis, penile curvature, spraying of urine, difficulty in urination\nTreatment: Surgical repair (hypospadias repair surgery), hormone therapy (in some cases), counseling and support for the child and family",
    "generated": "Hypospadias is a congenital malformation of the penis in which the urethral opening is located on the ventral side of the penis or on the coronal sulcus. It is one of the most common congenital malformations of the male genitalia, with an incidence of 1 in every 250\u2013300 newborn males. The symptoms of hypospadias include a downward-pointing penis, a shortened penis, a shortened scrotum, and a curved penis. In severe cases, the penis may appear small and the scrotum may be undeveloped. Treatment for hypospadias typically involves surgery, which is performed during infancy or early childhood. The type of surgery depends on the severity of the malformation and the age of the child. The goal of surgery is to create a functional and cosmetically acceptable penis. It is important to seek medical attention if you suspect that your child may have hypospadias, as early detection and treatment can help improve the chances of a successful outcome.",
